title: How to Use the Jev AI Model: A Step-by-Step Developer Guide
gist: A hands-on developer walkthrough for Jev AI's decision-model API: define State (text, JSON object, or array of text) plus typed Choice/Score/Noul Questions, call the POST https://thejevai.com/v1/systemone endpoint with a Bearer API key, and get back probability- and confidence-scored Answers keyed by question ID for application code to branch on, with repeated emphasis that probability is a routing signal, not a correctness guarantee.

themes.theme: Core interaction model and question types

insights.claim: The Jev AI model's interaction is built around three parts: State (text, JSON object, or array of text providing context), Questions (the decisions the application needs answered), and Answers (typed results the application code can branch on, sort, route, or review).
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Defines the exact API contract shape a developer or acquirer would need to integrate around or replicate if evaluating build-vs-buy.
insights.locator: What the Jev AI model does

insights.claim: Jev AI offers three question types: Choice (one option from a predefined set, for classification/routing), Score (a position on an ordered rubric, probability-weighted so it can fall between named levels, for severity/quality/intensity), and Noul (a 0-1 probability answer to a single yes-or-no proposition).
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Establishes the product's fixed primitive set, which bounds what kinds of decisions it can realistically serve and helps assess competitive differentiation versus a general LLM with a JSON schema.
insights.locator: Step 3: Select the right question type

insights.claim: Multiple questions can be sent against the same state in a single request and are evaluated in parallel, allowing one workflow (e.g., classification, scoring, and a safety judgment) to be resolved together instead of chaining separate model calls.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A latency/cost efficiency claim relevant to estimating per-decision unit economics versus making sequential LLM calls.
insights.quote: Multiple questions can use the same state and are evaluated in parallel.
insights.locator: Can I ask multiple questions in one request?

insights.claim: The guide instructs developers to start not by writing a prompt but by defining one bounded, testable decision (e.g., 'Which approved support team should handle this ticket?') rather than a vague goal like 'understand this customer.'
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A scoping discipline that reduces integration risk; useful diligence question for whether a team adopting Jev has a well-defined use case or is chasing hype.
insights.locator: Step 1: Choose one decision with a clear outcome

insights.claim: The article provides an 11-item production checklist covering defined answer space, minimal relevant state, single-purpose questions, complete Choice criteria, ordered Score levels, testable Noul propositions, server-side API key storage, safe fallbacks for timeouts/retries, tested probability thresholds, human review for high-impact actions, and logging that avoids exposing secrets.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Serves as an operational readiness checklist that investors/technical diligence teams can use to evaluate whether a company's Jev (or similar decision-model) integration is production-grade.

insights.claim: The production Jev API endpoint is POST https://thejevai.com/v1/systemone, authenticated via a Bearer token API key, with requests specifying a model field (example shown: 'jev-latest') plus state and questions in the JSON body.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A concrete, verifiable technical fact about the product's integration surface, useful for competitive/technical due diligence.
insights.locator: Step 5: Call the Jev API from your server

insights.claim: A sample API response shows the resolved model version as 'jev-1.13.0' and includes per-question answers with probabilities and confidence (e.g., a Choice answer for 'department' with billing probability 0.94 and confidence 0.92) plus token usage counts (input_tokens: 180, output_tokens: 24).
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete reference point for the product's current model version and token-based usage metering, useful for cost modeling.
insights.locator: Step 6: Use the structured response in application code

insights.claim: As of this guide, Jev AI's supported state inputs are limited to text, JSON objects, and arrays of text; images, audio, and video are not listed as supported direct inputs, so developers must convert or summarize such media before sending it as state.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A concrete current product limitation that bounds near-term use cases (e.g., no native multimodal moderation or vision-based routing) and is a useful watch-item for future roadmap/feature announcements.
insights.quote: Images, audio, and video are not listed as supported direct inputs, so convert or summarize those sources in your application before asking a decision question.
insights.locator: Can I send images, audio, or video as state?

insights.claim: The guide recommends a four-tier automation policy based on Jev's probability/confidence output: high probability plus low risk continues automatically; medium probability or an unfamiliar case collects more context; high-risk action or low confidence requires human approval; unsupported or malformed input returns an error or safe fallback.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A reusable risk-tiering framework for any team building automation atop probabilistic model outputs, not specific to Jev alone.
insights.locator: How to use probability and confidence safely

insights.claim: The article explicitly states probability and confidence scores are not a guarantee that a business decision is correct, and that a threshold tuned for support routing may be inappropriate for payments, account access, or destructive tools.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: A vendor-content risk disclosure that should temper claims of Jev's reliability for high-stakes automated decisions; important for assessing liability exposure of adopters.
insights.quote: Probability and confidence are useful for routing, ranking, and escalation, but they are not a guarantee that a business decision is correct.
insights.locator: How to use probability and confidence safely

insights.claim: The guide states Jev should not be allowed to silently delete data, send a payment, publish content, or call a sensitive tool without an application-level permission check, placing responsibility for high-risk actions on the integrating application rather than the model.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Clarifies where liability/control is expected to sit in a Jev-based system, relevant to assessing governance risk for enterprise buyers.
insights.quote: Jev should not silently delete data, send a payment, publish content, or call a sensitive tool without an application-level permission check.
insights.locator: Step 6: Use the structured response in application code

insights.claim: The guide's closing cross-promotion links to other articles by the same author published within roughly 24-48 hours, including one comparing 'Jev ai vs djev vs Laya vs OpenJev vs SemIf' and another on building agents with Jev AI, consistent with a coordinated content-marketing campaign around a single product's launch rather than independent evaluation.
insights.speaker: bna
insights.so_what: Investors should discount claims in this piece as vendor-aligned promotional content rather than independent technical journalism when assessing Jev AI's real-world traction or quality.
